I.1.1.1.1.title: A. Being
I.1.1.1.1.text: Being, pure being — without any further determination. In its indeterminate immediacy it is equal only to itself, and also not unequal with respect to an other; it has no difference within it, nor again without it. (Miller, p. 82)

I.1.1.1.2.title: B. Nothing
I.1.1.1.2.text: Nothing, pure nothing: it is simply equality with itself, complete emptiness, absence of all determination and content — undifferentiatedness in itself. (Miller, p. 82)

I.1.1.1.3.title: C. Becoming
I.1.1.1.3.text: Pure Being and pure Nothing are, therefore, the same. What is the truth is neither Being nor Nothing, but that Being does not pass over, but has passed over, into Nothing; and Nothing does not pass over, but has passed over, into Being. (Miller, pp. 82–83, 105)

I.1.1.2.1.1.title: a. Determinate Being in General
I.1.1.2.1.1.text: Determinate being is being with a determinateness which is posited as a moment of being itself — not as an external mark, but as the very form in which being is present. (Miller, pp. 109–111)

I.2.1.1.1.title: A. The Essential and the Unessential
I.2.1.1.1.text: Essence is being that has returned into itself. It is not immediate being, but being as sublated — being which is what it is only through the negation of immediacy. (Miller, pp. 341–342)
